title: Zoom AI Receptionist: Pricing, features, and limitations in 2026
summary: Dive into Zoom AI Receptionist features. Learn what it does, what it costs, and how it compares to alternatives like Quo’s Sona.
body_markdown:
Zoom has come a long way from its origins as a video conferencing platform. It’s built a complete business phone system and continues to expand its capabilities. In August 2025,[Zoom Phone](https://www.quo.com/blog/zoom-phone-alternatives/) released an[AI receptionist](https://www.quo.com/product/ai/receptionist) . There’s even a standalone version that connects with third-party phone platforms.


Zoom’s AI Receptionist answers calls 24/7, books appointments, and routes callers. It costs $25 a month with annual billing for 100 minutes as a standalone feature, or $0.25 a minute if added on to an existing Zoom Phone plan.


If you’re looking for a basic AI receptionist and you already use Zoom Phone, then this AI receptionist could work for you. But it’s tough to set up, can’t handle complex conversations, and can get expensive quickly.


This article explains everything you should know about Zoom’s AI receptionist. We’ll cover pricing, fees, and limitations, and we’ll show you a better alternative for a virtual receptionist.


##


What is the Zoom AI receptionist?


The official name of Zoom’s AI agent is the Zoom Virtual Agent Receptionist. You may also hear it referred to as ZVA Receptionist.


ZVA is an AI-powered tool that answers questions, books appointments, and routes calls to team members. It integrates directly with Zoom Phone with an add-on. It’s also available as a standalone service as of July 2026.


##


What can the Zoom AI receptionist do?


Here’s a short list of what Zoom Virtual Agent Receptionist is capable of:


- **24/7 call handling.** It’s always available to answer calls
- **Natural language processing.** Understands and responds to regular speech
- [Call transfers](https://www.quo.com/product/call-forwarding/call-transfer) **.** Route callers to team members with context
- **Schedule appointments.** Book meetings and generate meeting links. Integrates with Zoom Scheduler, Google Calendar, Microsoft, and Calendly
- [SMS messaging](https://www.quo.com/product/messaging) **.** Sends appointment reminders and links during text conversations
- **Support for multiple languages.** Supported languages include English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, and Japanese
- **Lead capture.** Can identify caller intent and capture lead details
- **Custom greetings.** Write your own custom greetings for the agent to perform
- **Answer common questions.** Pulls information from a knowledge base and gives it to the caller

##


How much does the Zoom AI receptionist cost?


Zoom offers two AI receptionist plans: a standalone plan and a bundled plan for existing Zoom Phone users.


The standalone plan costs $25 per month with annual billing. The bundled plan requires a Zoom Phone subscription of any tier, plus $10 per user per month.


Keep in mind this doesn’t include all Zoom Phone platform costs. You can get the exact numbers in our[Zoom Phone pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/zoom-phone-pricing/) breakdown.


Zoom Virtual Agent Receptionist Standalone Zoom Phone with AI receptionist


$25 per month billed annually $10 per user per month + $0.25 per minute


The standalone plan includes 100 minutes of use per month. The bundled plan is charged differently: $0.25 per minute unless you purchase bundled free minutes in increments of 100, 250, or 500 minutes per month.


Another thing to keep in mind: Zoom doesn’t publicly advertise an overage rate for the standalone plan. Instead, you have to either:


- Buy a bundled “Minute Tier” from the account control panel
- Buy a one-time “Virtual Receptionist Minute Pack” to top up your account


Unfortunately, Zoom doesn’t advertise the prices of either the Minute Tier or the Virtual Receptionist Minute Pack. The only way to get a quote is to contact sales.


##


Hidden costs of the Zoom AI receptionist


The Zoom AI receptionist *can* be an option for handling high call volumes. But it can be very expensive for small businesses.


Here’s why:


### Costs make Zoom AI receptionist impractical


The pricing model for Zoom’s AI agent isn’t friendly to growing businesses. Most small businesses look for AI receptionists to help manage high call volumes. But if it fields *too many* calls, it can become too expensive.


Per-call pricing would make more sense in these situations. That way, you’re not penalized for something you can’t control, like the length of a call.


But that’s not how Zoom manages its AI pricing model.


You get 100 minutes per month, but that doesn’t handle many calls. If the average call is five minutes, only 20 of your AI agent’s calls are free. A busy business can easily field 20 calls in a single day — sometimes by lunch. And if you get a talkative customer or the AI struggles to handle a request, you can burn through your free minutes fast.


And if you get an unexpected wave of incoming calls, your AI receptionist usage costs will spike accordingly.


Of course, every business’s phone traffic is different. High call volumes for one might be light for another. To get a better idea of costs, we’ve calculated ranges in the table below:*


Monthly ZVA minutes used Base cost for one user $0.25 per minute overage fee True ZVA cost for the month


100 $10 $0 $10


300 $10 $75 $85


500 $10 $125 $135


700 $10 $175 $185


**The calculation above is for the bundled monthly plan, which requires at least one Zoom Phone subscription.*


Keep in mind that Zoom’s overage costs for the standalone plan are difficult to predict because Zoom doesn’t provide this information. That brings us to our next point:


### Zoom hides the true overage cost


Beyond the advertised $0.25-per-minute rate, none of ZVA’s extra costs are publicly available. As far as we can tell, the standalone plan has no per-minute overage fee. The agent simply stops working until you purchase more minutes through one of two methods:


- **Minute Tier.** A monthly allowance of additional free minutes, available in 100-, 250-, or 500-minute increments. Zoom doesn’t say how much each tier costs. But it *does* say the price differs between standalone plans and bundle plans.
- **Virtual Receptionist Minute Pack.** A one-time purchase of additional minutes credited to your account. Zoom doesn’t say how much it is or how many minutes you’re buying. It doesn’t even say whether there are different packs with different amounts of minutes.


### You can’t customize call routing


Zoom AI doesn’t let you control *when* your AI agent answers calls. This limits the ways you can use the AI. For example, you can’t use the AI as a backup when your reps aren’t available. You also can’t use it as a menu option where callers can choose the AI for themselves.


Zoom’s virtual agent will always pick up the phone first.


You can customize what ZVA does after it answers, like transferring to a team member or answering questions. But you can’t decide *when* or *why* it answers.


This[call routing](https://www.quo.com/product/call-routing) flow can get expensive fast.


### Complicated setup


Many past[Zoom AI customers](https://www.g2.com/products/zoom-virtual-agent/reviews) say the Virtual Agent Receptionist is difficult to set up and train. Some say they needed technical expertise to get the most out of the system. Several reviews also discuss how hard it is to set up, customize, and connect with third-party app integrations.


This reviewer mentions an[integration latency](https://www.g2.com/products/zoom-virtual-agent/reviews/zoom-virtual-agent-review-12864000) across third-party CRMs that disrupted their workflow:


*“ZVA’s configuration depth, while powerful, introduces steep initial complexity, elevating cognitive load during onboarding. Integration latency across third-party CRMs produces measurable workflow disruption. Pricing scales aggressively with volume, compressing ROI at enterprise levels.”* —[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/zoom-virtual-agent/reviews/zoom-virtual-agent-review-12864000)


### Complex conversations are a challenge


The ZVA Receptionist can struggle with complex questions. This is especially true if it involves a[non-English language](https://www.g2.com/products/zoom-virtual-agent/reviews/zoom-virtual-agent-review-5151167) . Callers may get frustrated and react negatively.


As one reviewer wrote:


*“Unfortunately, we’ve seen many mismatches and accuracy issues for the languages my operation is active in. These are Dutch and French markets. These issues have been raised several times, but until now, no real improvements were made. This language-accuracy issue is leading to less satisfactory solutions to our customers, and probably our self-service ratios could’ve been higher.”* —[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/zoom-virtual-agent/reviews/zoom-virtual-agent-review-5151167)


##


4 Biggest Zoom Phone limitations


Signing up for the Zoom Phone bundle also means dealing with some limitations.


These include:


- **Expensive outbound calling.** Zoom’s base plan charges for outbound calls until you upgrade to a higher plan. Most modern VoIP phone systems include outbound calling in their base plans.
- **No international MMS.** Zoom Phone doesn’t allow you to send MMS internationally, including video files. That means you can’t ask customers for screenshots or recordings unless you set up a Zoom meeting.
- **Confusing setup.** Multiple[Zoom customers](https://www.g2.com/products/zoom-zoom-phone/reviews/zoom-phone-review-9662817) have reported issues navigating and customizing their Zoom web portal. This also suggests that you may need to dedicate time each week to managing the phone system.
- **Team collaboration challenges.** You can’t send or receive messages from a shared phone number without paying extra for the Customer Engagement pack. Further, only 10 team members can be on shared lines on a single plan. This could get frustrating as your team grows.

##


**FAQ**


****Do I need a Zoom Phone subscription to access the Zoom Virtual Agent Receptionist?****


No, you don’t need a Zoom Phone subscription to access its AI voice agent. You can use a standalone option alongside other independent phone systems.


****Does the Zoom Phone AI Receptionist have a free trial?****


You can test Zoom Phone’s AI receptionist when you sign up for their seven-day free trial. You’ll get 100 minutes to test features like custom greetings, lead qualification, and the ability to answer FAQs. Unspent minutes expire once the trial period ends.


****Does the Zoom AI Receptionist allow me to set up virtual chats?****


Zoom Phone’s AI receptionist is a voice-only tool. You’ll have to set up a separate chat-capable AI agent in the Zoom AI Studio if you want AI to help manage customer chats.


****What is the Zoom AI Studio?****


Zoom AI Studio lets you create AI agents like the Receptionist. It’s available on the ZoomMate plan, starting at $16.67 per user per month, billed annually. With it, you can create workflows with access to third-party applications, then add workflow templates to your library.
